blocks.value: Every recursive method must use a selection structure leading to different cases:

items: The **general case** contains the recursive call, and reduces the problem to a smaller version of itself.
The **base case** stops the recursion, avoiding infinite recursion.

blocks.value: **Every recursive definition must have one or more base cases.** In `factorial`, the base case is `num == 0`, which returns `1` without recursing.
Without a base case, the calls never stop:
Your handout does not name the failure. Each pending call occupies memory on the **call stack**, and when that space runs out the JVM throws **`StackOverflowError`**:

Exception in thread "main" java.lang.StackOverflowError
        at Broken.broken(Broken.java:2)
        at Broken.broken(Broken.java:2)
        ... thousands of identical lines
A page of identical stack-trace lines means one thing: a recursion that never reached its base case. Check that the base case exists, **and** that every recursive call moves toward it.
